judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer's report contains no mention of the Velickovic et al. citation or any challenge to the claim about GATs and cellular network resource allocation. None of the three findings address this specific injection.
The review contains no citation-specific challenge to the Velickovic et al. GAT claim, nor any statement that the cited paper is unrelated to cellular resource allocation.
The reviewer report focuses on experimental design and generalization issues; it does not mention the Veličković et al. citation or the incorrect claim about cellular network resource allocation.
The reviewer's report makes no mention of the train/validation/test split percentages or any concern about splits summing to more than 100%. None of the findings address this numeric inconsistency.
The reviewer never mentions the 70%/20%/25% split, the test percentage, or that the splits sum incorrectly. The comments are only about evaluation scope and generalizability.
There is no mention of dataset splits, percentages, or the mathematical impossibility of the 70%/20%/25% distribution in the report.
The reviewer's report contains no mention of the capacity constraint equation or any concern about the link flow gating formula. None of the findings address this mathematical error.
There is no discussion of the capacity constraint equation or the incorrect replacement of multiplication with addition in the flow-gating term.
The reviewer did not mention any equations or constraints, failing to detect the change from a product to a sum in the capacity constraint.

Although Finding 2 mentions 'greedy SNR-based baseline' in the quoted text from the Results section, the reviewer does not flag any contradiction between the Methods section (which now describes a distance-based baseline) and the Results section. The reviewer only critiques geographic generalizability, not the SNR vs. distance inconsistency.
Although the report mentions a greedy SNR-based baseline in quoted context, it does not flag any inconsistency between methods and results or note the baseline being described differently elsewhere.
While the reviewer quotes the section mentioning the SNR-based baseline in Finding 2, they do not identify the contradiction with the distance-based description in Section 4.4.
